mcqs.q: In the Goa free-roaming dog (FRD) survey, what proportion of respondents reported feeding FRD?
mcqs.e: 37% fed FRD, with dog owners and Hindus most likely to feed.

mcqs.q: Which problem was most commonly attributed to free-roaming dogs?
mcqs.e: Barking was the most frequently reported FRD-associated problem.

mcqs.q: What was respondents' preferred solution for managing FRD?
mcqs.e: Impounding FRD in shelters was the preferred solution despite majority agreement that FRD belong in communities.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about the Community Dog Program methodology across the five Paraná municipalities?
o: It proved applicable for implementation in all five
It succeeded in only one municipality
It required lethal control to function
mcqs.e: The methodology was applicable in all five municipalities and could support a guiding protocol for others.

mcqs.q: Which were identified as main implementation challenges?
o: Inadequate caretaker handling of food/water and limited secretariat structure
mcqs.e: Inadequate caretaker feeding/watering and limited secretariat human resources/structure were the principal challenges.

mcqs.q: In Piraquara, what percentage of enrolled dogs lacked a fixed shelter?
mcqs.e: 75% (15/20) of Piraquara dogs had no fixed shelter but met other criteria.

mcqs.q: Which method does the article identify as the most effective and humane for controlling free-roaming cats?
mcqs.e: TNR is described as the most effective and humane control method, enhanced by adoption and public education.

mcqs.q: How does the article characterize lethal control and removal of cats?
mcqs.e: Veterinarians oppose lethal control/removal as ineffective and unethical.

mcqs.q: How does the article describe the public health risks associated with cats?
mcqs.e: Veterinary experts assert the public health risks of cats are often overstated.

mcqs.q: What was the main finding regarding caregivers affected by the Port of Newcastle cat shooting?
o: Negative impacts on psychological health and quality of life
mcqs.e: Caregivers showed strong cat bonds and negative psychological/quality-of-life impacts from lethal management.

mcqs.q: What management approach did the authors recommend for the future?
o: A care-centred approach aiding neutering and, where possible, adoption
mcqs.e: A care-centred approach (neutering/adoption) was recommended to improve welfare and reduce caregiver harm.

mcqs.q: What legislative change did the study recommend?
o: Revising legislation distinguishing domestic from feral cats
mcqs.e: Authors urged revising laws that distinguish domestic from feral cats to prevent unnecessary killing of domestic cats.

mcqs.q: What level of public support for TNR emerged from the Weibo analysis?
mcqs.e: TNR received high support in public discussion of stray cats.

mcqs.q: How did knowledge of stray cats' ecological impacts relate to support for lethal control?
mcqs.e: Greater knowledge of ecological impacts was positively correlated with support for lethal control.

mcqs.q: What data source did the study use to gauge public opinion?
mcqs.e: User-generated Weibo content was analyzed via natural language processing.

mcqs.q: In which season were free-roaming cat home ranges significantly larger in Cape Town?
mcqs.e: Home ranges and roaming distances were significantly larger in summer than winter.

mcqs.q: What buffer width around conservation areas did the authors recommend to reduce cat impacts on native fauna?
mcqs.e: Results suggest cat buffers of at least ~600 m around conservation areas.

mcqs.q: Which cats made the most extensive use of protected areas in summer?
o: Urban cats >150 m from the edge
mcqs.e: In summer all seven urban-edge cats used protected areas, versus only one of seven urban cats.

mcqs.q: What were the primary intervention areas described by MHA Nation participants regarding rez dogs?
o: Culturally relevant information sharing, improved animal control, and improved access to veterinary care
mcqs.e: Participants emphasized culturally relevant information, better animal control, and improved access to veterinary/animal services.

mcqs.q: Which method did the study use?
o: Semi-structured interviews analyzed via hermeneutical phenomenology
mcqs.e: Fourteen one-hour semi-structured interviews were analyzed with Gadamer's hermeneutical phenomenology.

mcqs.q: How did the authors characterize prior research on rez dogs and Indigenous communities?
mcqs.e: The article states research on free-roaming dogs and Indigenous communities is extremely limited.

mcqs.q: Which methods did the Sydney study use to quantify free-roaming cat abundance?
mcqs.e: Motion-capture cameras on volunteer properties plus transect drives quantified cat abundance.

mcqs.q: Which local government area had the higher free-roaming cat density?
mcqs.e: Campbelltown had higher density (0.31 vs 0.21 cats/ha) than the Blue Mountains.

mcqs.q: Where were more wildlife events captured?
mcqs.e: More wildlife events were captured in the Blue Mountains (5580) than Campbelltown (2697).

mcqs.q: Which cat subpopulation most influenced overall UK population dynamics in the model?
mcqs.e: Owned cats, the majority of the population, had the greatest influence on overall dynamics.

mcqs.q: Population growth rate was most sensitive to which vital rates?
mcqs.e: Growth rate was most influenced by owned cat survival and fecundity.

mcqs.q: What did simulations show about neutering owned cats at a younger age?
o: Sufficient to reduce overall growth regardless of neutering prevalence
mcqs.e: Neutering owned cats younger reduced overall population growth irrespective of overall prevalence.

mcqs.q: Indoor management of cats was associated with which outcome?
o: Greater variety/frequency of care practices and a more positive relationship
mcqs.e: Indoor management was linked to more frequent/varied care practices and a more positive cat-caretaker relationship.

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about the cat-caretaker relationship?
o: Indoor-management caretakers were more likely to have a positive relationship
mcqs.e: Indoor-management caretakers were more likely to have a positive relationship with their cats.

mcqs.q: What method did the study use?
mcqs.e: Data came from an online questionnaire of 114 owners in two Brazilian municipalities.

mcqs.q: What did the assistive-centred urban cat management approach provide to caregivers?
mcqs.e: The approach offered free sterilization and preventative healthcare for semi-owned and owned cats.

mcqs.q: How did the assistive-centred approach affect caregiver quality of life?
mcqs.e: Caregivers reported a positive impact on quality of life and improved cat welfare after sterilization.

mcqs.q: With which philosophy did the authors say this approach aligns?
mcqs.e: The assistive-centred approach is aligned with the One Welfare philosophy.

mcqs.q: What was the approximate prevalence of chronic gingivostomatitis among the 345 TNR feral cats studied?
mcqs.e: 92 of 345 feral cats (about 27%) had chronic gingivostomatitis.

mcqs.q: Prevalence and severity of chronic gingivostomatitis were associated with which finding?
mcqs.e: Prevalence and severity were associated with tongue lesions, suggesting an infectious link.

mcqs.q: Which factors did NOT affect prevalence in this study?
mcqs.e: Weight and sex did not affect prevalence.
